correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge1\) and \(0<q<1\) the independent insertion code is proved from Mallows weights. The exact event equivalence with forbidden deep insertions and adjacent unit insertions follows by induction on largest inserted value. Enumeration of path matchings gives \(F_n(q)\). Characteristic roots of its second-order recurrence yield the claimed uniform logarithmic expansion as q goes to zero. Marked Poisson convergence is proved through mixed factorial moments: isolated mark choices give homogeneous intensity c per type, and overlapping B clusters contribute \(O(nq^3)\) or less, while incompatible A/B events have probability zero. This covers \(c=0\) and \(c>0\) without claiming a false finite-to-infinite certification; 138780 finite assertion events independently test structural and partition identities.

originality.rationale: Distinct from known standard Mallows insertion code, single-pattern avoidance results, and fixed-q cycle Gaussian limits: the new claim is the two-type spatial Poisson threshold at \(nq_n^2\) for a jointly constrained path-matching permutation class, plus the uniform exact probability asymptotic. The comparisons use primary source theorem statements and implication differences. Incomplete coverage of all alternate historical terminology is retained as a risk.
residual_risks: A closed-form weighted path-matching distribution is elementary enough that it may exist in a prior combinatorial table under a different name.

value.rationale: A natural near-identity ranking model has order \(nq\) single adjacent swap moves, but remains a product of disjoint adjacent swaps until order \(nq^2\) local collisions and deep insertions appear. The exact finite-n probability and homogeneous two-mark Poisson process give a sharp square-root parameter boundary, with two distinct failure types and their spatial locations. This is not simply a q-factorial reparametrization or a fixed-n census, and yields interpretable structural information unavailable from the marginal inversion count alone.
